commands.command: python3 /tmp/walk_4010b0.py  (script below; run from the repository or /tmp)
commands.script:
from capstone import *
PATH='/Users/haseeb-mir/Downloads/IGI/igi.exe'
data=open(PATH,'rb').read()
md=Cs(CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_32); md.skipdata=True
ins={i.address:i for i in md.disasm(data[0x1000:0x133000],0x401000) if i.mnemonic!='(data)'}

def is_jmp(i): return i.mnemonic=='jmp' and i.op_str.startswith('0x')
def is_jcc(i): return i.mnemonic.startswith('j') and i.mnemonic!='jmp' and i.op_str.startswith('0x')

reach=set(); calls=[]; tails=set(); leaders={0x4010B0}
work=[0x4010B0]
while work:
    a=work.pop()
    while a in ins and a not in reach:
        i=ins[a]; reach.add(a)
        if i.mnemonic.startswith('ret'): break
        if is_jmp(i):
            t=int(i.op_str,16); tails.add(t); leaders.add(t); work.append(t); break
        if is_jcc(i):
            t=int(i.op_str,16); leaders.add(t); work.append(t)
            nxt=i.address+i.size; leaders.add(nxt); a=nxt; continue
        if i.mnemonic=='call' and i.op_str.startswith('0x'):
            calls.append((a,int(i.op_str,16)))
        a=i.address+i.size
starts=sorted(x for x in leaders if x in reach)
blocks=[]
for idx,s in enumerate(starts):
    nxt=starts[idx+1] if idx+1<len(starts) else None
    end=s; last=None
    while end in reach:
        i=ins[end]; last=i; end=i.address+i.size
        if i.mnemonic.startswith('ret') or is_jmp(i) or is_jcc(i): break
        if nxt is not None and end==nxt: break
    blocks.append((s,end))
print('conventional_blocks',len(blocks))
print('block_ranges',[(hex(s),hex(e)) for s,e in blocks])
print('instructions',len(reach))
print('bytes',sum(ins[a].size for a in reach))
print('direct_calls',len(calls))
print('unique_direct_call_targets',len(set(t for _,t in calls)))
print('unique_cascade_call_targets',len(set(t for a,t in calls if a>=0x402C40)))
print('tail_targets',[hex(x) for x in sorted(tails)])
print('terminal_rets',[hex(a) for a in reach if ins[a].mnemonic.startswith('ret')])

independent_reanalysis.detail: The retail image was re-read byte-exactly with objdump and capstone, then re-analysed with Binary Ninja MCP, radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1. Binary Ninja is the only decompiler used in this corrected pass. The prior Ghidra pass is retained only as superseded historical evidence.

observed_facts.fact: The hashed image is PE32, machine i386, preferred image base 0x00400000, Windows GUI subsystem, .text at VA 0x00401000 with virtual size 0x00132000. SHA-256 is dea34892d417715873ea61d7b2ba5556655f1ad65385104348146f9679915a01 and MD5 is 9d8ebb7f28a1be56a8626dd5948826e4.

The function at 0x004010B0 is 28 bytes, 0x004010B0-0x004010CB, with raw bytes e8ab09000085c0740ee8c217000050e82c05000083c404e9741b0000. The next byte at 0x004010CC is 0x90 padding. Binary Ninja reports 3 basic blocks and 28 bytes; radare2 confirms the entry's 8 instructions.

The entry body is: call 0x00401A60; test eax,eax; je 0x004010C7; call 0x00402880; push eax; call 0x004015F0; add esp,4; jmp 0x00402C40. The conditional branch skips the 0x00402880/0x004015F0 pair when 0x00401A60 returns 0; 0x00402C40 runs either way. The function ends in an unconditional jmp, not a ret.

Binary Ninja partitions the entry into blocks 0x004010B0-0x004010B9 (9 bytes), 0x004010B9-0x004010C7 (14 bytes) and 0x004010C7-0x004010CC (5 bytes). Complexity is 3 blocks, 3 edges and 4 call edges including the tail jump; total bytes 28.

The entry reads no stack arguments (no ESP/EBP-relative memory operand) and has one balanced push/add esp pair. It has no ret: it tail-jumps to 0x00402C40, so the value the caller sees in EAX comes from the tail chain. The direct caller at 0x0048F9D4 discards EAX; no source-level return type is proven.

There is exactly one direct E8 call to 0x004010B0, at 0x0048F9D4 in the WM_DESTROY branch of 0x0048F970. There are no E9/EB jumps and no stored dword literal equal to 0x004010B0. Binary Ninja additionally reports a fallthrough predecessor at 0x004010AF from 0x004010A0, which calls Camera_ApplyBandFilter_3(0x54F8E0,1) and then falls through NOPs into 0x004010B0; radare2 axt reports only the direct call.

The tail target 0x00402C40 is a single 775-byte basic block, 0x00402C40-0x00402F46, with 154 direct call instructions and a final jmp 0x00508F90 at 0x00402F42. Binary Ninja reports 1 block, 155 callee rows (154 calls + 1 tail jump), total bytes 775. It is not a 306-byte or 5-block function.

The tail chain continues through 0x00508F90 (10 bytes, 1 block, 1 direct call + jmp), 0x00518550 (365 bytes, 1 block, 72 direct calls + jmp), 0x005302A0 (35 bytes, 1 block, 6 direct calls + jmp), 0x00530A20 (95 bytes, 1 block, 18 direct calls + jmp), 0x005311F0 (10 bytes, 1 block, 1 direct call + jmp), 0x005323D0 (15 bytes, 1 block, 2 direct calls + jmp), 0x005323F0 (10 bytes, 1 block, 1 direct call + jmp), 0x00532490 (120 bytes, 1 block, 23 direct calls + jmp) and ends at the single-byte plain C3 ret at 0x004C1780.

Across the entry and the tail chain, the conventional partition has 13 blocks (3 entry + 10 tail-reached), 296 instructions, 1464 bytes (entry 28, tail-reached 1436), 281 direct call instructions, 261 unique direct call targets and 258 unique cascade call targets (excluding the entry's three calls). The 258 figure is unique targets, not call instructions.
observed_facts.evidence: C10; BN per-block callee rows; r2 out-degree 281

observed_facts.fact: There are no ESP- or EBP-relative memory operands anywhere in the reachable chain, no pops, one push (0x004010BE push eax) balanced by add esp,4, and a terminal plain c3 ret at 0x004C1780. No ret imm exists on the reachable path.
The chain has a single conditional branch (the entry's je at 0x004010B7); after the entry, control proceeds by unconditional tail jumps only. No loop back-edge was found.

Fresh radare2 6.2.0 recovery of 0x004010B0 merges the tail chain: realsz 1463, 12 blocks, 295 instructions, out-degree 281, in-degree 1; its size field 1250392 is an analysis artifact and is not used. The missing 1 byte/block/instruction relative to the capstone total is the terminal ret at 0x004C1780. angr recovers 0x004010B0 as 0x5b7 bytes and 293 call-delimited blocks; it does not recover 0x00402C40 separately.

In the WM_DESTROY branch of 0x0048F970 the observed order is: push 1 at 0x0048F9C5; store 0 to 0x005C8DE8 at 0x0048F9C7; call USER32!ShowCursor at 0x0048F9CE; call 0x004010B0 at 0x0048F9D4 with EAX discarded; push 0 at 0x0048F9D9 and call USER32!PostQuitMessage at 0x0048F9DB; pop registers, xor eax,eax, ret 0x10 at 0x0048F9E1-0x0048F9E7.

Binary Ninja's names QTask_DispatchEvent (0x004010B0), Flow_DeleteHandler (0x00402C40) and the tail-block names are database annotations, not retail PE symbols. They are not used as behavior evidence.

The earlier record's address-level tail_reached_cascade label conflated the 0x00402C40 775-byte block with the whole tail chain. The corrected separation is: 28-byte entry at 0x004010B0; 775-byte first tail block at 0x00402C40; 1464-byte reachable region ending at 0x004C1780.

hypotheses.hypothesis: 0x004010B0 is a shutdown/dispatch entry that optionally runs two cleanup calls and then always enters the common tail region at 0x00402C40.
hypotheses.basis: The branch skips only the 0x00402880/0x004015F0 pair, while the tail jump is unconditional.
hypotheses.status: strongly suggested by control flow; the meaning of the three directly called functions is unknown

hypotheses.hypothesis: 0x00402C40 and its tail chain tear down engine subsystems.
hypotheses.basis: The large ordered call cascade and its invocation from the WM_DESTROY branch.
hypotheses.status: descriptive only; subsystem identity is unresolved

hypotheses.hypothesis: 'engine teardown native' is a descriptive label for 0x004010B0 plus this chain, not a recovered symbol.

unresolved.item: Which subsystems the cascade tears down is unresolved. The 281 direct calls were counted but not classified; no DirectDraw, Direct3D, sound or timer attribution is made.
The semantics of 0x00401A60, 0x00402880 and 0x004015F0 are unknown, so the condition and the two skipped calls are not interpreted.
The return value and source-level return type of 0x004010B0 are not established; the direct caller discards EAX and the entry ends in a tail jump.
Register-based arguments supplied to the cascade calls (if any) were not analysed; only stack arguments were ruled out.

The earlier supplied figures of 306 bytes, 5 basic blocks and a plain ret inside a 306-byte function are not reproduced at 0x004010B0. Binary Ninja also shows that 0x00402C40 is 775 bytes and 1 block, so the 306/5 figures do not describe 0x00402C40 either. Their origin remains unresolved and they are not asserted.
The relationship between 0x004010A0's fallthrough into 0x004010B0 and the direct call from 0x0048F9D4 is not fully classified; why 0x004010A0 has no ret of its own was not analysed.
The meaning of the 258 unique cascade call targets is unresolved; the names shown by Binary Ninja are database annotations.

limitations: Static analysis only. No runtime, behavioural or paired retail/candidate evidence exists for this record, and none is implied.

The earlier record wrongly attributed 306 bytes, 5 basic blocks, roughly 258 calls and a plain ret to 0x004010B0. The corrected facts are: 28 bytes, 3 basic blocks, 3 direct calls plus one tail jmp at 0x004010B0; the tail target 0x00402C40 is 775 bytes and 1 basic block with 154 direct calls plus one tail jmp; the full reachable chain is 1464 bytes, 13 conventional blocks, 296 instructions and 281 direct call instructions, with the terminal plain ret at 0x004C1780. The 306/5 figures remain unresolved and are not asserted anywhere in this record.
The 258 figure is the number of unique direct call targets in the cascade, not the number of call instructions (281), and it is not a property of the 28-byte entry function.
The tail chain is followed structurally through its unconditional jumps. The 281 calls were counted but not semantically classified; no subsystem attribution is made.
Binary Ninja's function and callee names are database annotations, not retail symbols; they are not used as behavior evidence.

radare2's function recovery merges the tail chain and excludes the terminal 1-byte ret; its size field 1250392 is an analysis artifact. The exact reachable totals come from the capstone walk and BN per-block counts, with radare2's out-degree 281 as an independent call-count check.
angr's 293 blocks are call-delimited, not conventional basic blocks; angr does not recover 0x00402C40 separately. angr is used only as an independent size/reachability check.
No candidate source was reviewed or compared, and no CFG-similarity score or structural-verification claim is made.
The function name is descriptive only; the retail PE provides no source-level name for this address.
